task: ai-bookkeeper (flagship row 1): BUILDABLE item, tesseract's four readings of CORD train shards 1-3 for the five-reading vote
errors: A combined Bash call that started a background OCR job with '&' plus a heredoc looked like it failed (the helper script and a folder seemed missing; its log stayed empty) but the job was running; I started a duplicate run and stopped it once I saw both in ps. Use run_in_background for long jobs, not '&' inside a foreground call.

doc_friction.issue: ai-bookkeeper's buildable item said 'tesseract's four on CORD shards 1-3 for the five-reading vote', but eval/second-ocr-engine-2026-11-17.md had already scored that vote on train (510) with an older parser; the open part was re-scoring it with today's parser, which took reading two eval docs to work out.

notes: Read CORD train shards 1-3 (600 photos) with RapidOCR (reproduced 539/583) and tesseract's four (~100 min, 4 cores). The five-reading vote read 526, below RapidOCR alone: 19 of 21 losses were an unconfirmed tesseract majority overriding RapidOCR's right total. New parseReceiptPasses option `lead` (CLI --rapidocr --four-pass and the page pass it): an outvoting total needs the receipt's arithmetic. Chosen on train among 3 variants (simplest, 542) before other sets were read. Train 526->542, tax 205->209 of 267; validation 87->87 (tax 40/3/4 -> 41/1/5); test 83->83 CLI, page 84->83 (scored once); SRD 186->188, tax 163->161; page wrong-with-no-warning unchanged (train 14, SRD 2). The gain is mostly on the set where it was chosen; on held-out sets it is about level, and the claim made is that the five-reading mode no longer loses totals against RapidOCR alone. Tests: node --test over the venture, 3346/3346 before the new file; receipt-lead-vote.test.mjs 4/4; run_venture_tests.py ai-bookkeeper rerun before merge. Page scored with Python RapidOCR as lead, not the JS port.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
